questions.question: In which year did Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan assume office as the first Vice President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1952**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan** assumed office as the first Vice President of India in **1952**.
 
• He served as Vice President from 1952 to 1962, and later became the President of India from 1962 to 1967.
 
• Dr. Radhakrishnan was a distinguished scholar, philosopher, and statesman, and his contributions to education and philosophy are widely recognized.
 
• He played a significant role in shaping India's educational system and promoting Indian philosophy on the global stage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was born on 5th September 1888, which is celebrated as **Teacher's Day** in India in his honor.
 
• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1954.
 
• He was a strong advocate for education and believed that teachers play a crucial role in shaping the future of a nation.
 
• Dr. Radhakrishnan's works in philosophy include interpretations of Indian philosophy for Western audiences, and he emphasized the importance of understanding and dialogue between different cultures and religions.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement about Agar.

options.text: Agar is used to grow microbes.
Agar, one of the commercial products obtained from red algae, gelidium and gracilaria.
It is used as nutrient and source of fat of bacterial culture.
It is used in preparations of ice-creams and jellies.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is used as nutrient and source of fat of bacterial culture**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agar** is used to grow microbes.
 
• Agar, one of the commercial products obtained from red algae, **gelidium and gracilaria**.
 
• It is used in preparations of **ice-creams and jellies**.
 
• Contrary to option 3, **agar is not used as a nutrient and source of fat for bacterial culture**; it is primarily a solidifying agent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agar** is a gelatinous substance derived from red algae and is widely used in microbiology.
 
• It serves as a culture medium for various microorganisms due to its ability to remain solid at higher temperatures.
 
• Besides microbiology, agar is also used in the food industry for its gelling properties.
 
• The use of agar in bacterial culture is due to its inertness, meaning it does not provide nutrients but only serves as a solid base to support the growth of organisms when mixed with nutrient media.

questions.question: An argon positive ion fired towards east gets deflected towards south by a magnetic field. The direction of magnetic field is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**upward**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An argon positive ion fired towards the east gets deflected towards the south by a magnetic field.
 
• This deflection is explained by the right-hand rule for the force on a moving charge in a magnetic field.
 
• According to the right-hand rule, if the thumb points in the direction of the ion's velocity (east) and the fingers point in the direction of the magnetic field, the force (deflection) will be in the direction of the palm.
 
• Since the ion is deflected towards the south, the magnetic field must be directed **upward**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The right-hand rule is a mnemonic for understanding the direction of the magnetic force on a positive charge.
 
• In physics, the direction of a magnetic field can be determined using the right-hand rule by pointing the thumb of the right hand in the direction of the current and curling the fingers; the direction the fingers curl is the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• This principle is widely used in electromagnetism and helps in visualizing the direction of forces in a magnetic field.

questions.question: How many components of population change are there which are core to the domain of population studies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **3 core components** of population change in population studies.
 
• These components are **birth rate, death rate, and migration.**
 
• The **birth rate** refers to the number of live births per 1,000 people in a year.
 
• The **death rate** refers to the number of deaths per 1,000 people in a year.
 
• **Migration** includes both immigration (people moving into an area) and emigration (people moving out of an area).
 
• Understanding these components helps in analyzing population growth and demographic changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The study of population change is crucial for planning and policy-making in areas such as **healthcare, education, and housing.**
 
• Population studies also help in understanding the **socio-economic impacts** of population changes.
 
• Data on birth rates, death rates, and migration are typically collected through **censuses and surveys**.
 
• Changes in population can have significant effects on **economic development and resource allocation.**
 
• Population dynamics are influenced by a variety of factors including **economic conditions, cultural norms, and government policies.**

questions.question: In the context of movement of cells, exocytosis is the process by which:

options.text: cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane
cell death is brought about through a heavily regulated sequence of events
cells move waste materials from within the cell into the extracellular fluid
a cell takes in the fluids along with dissolved small molecules

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cells move waste materials from within the cell into the extracellular fluid**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exocytosis** is a process used by cells to move materials from within the cell into the extracellular fluid.
 
• This process involves vesicles containing waste materials or other substances fusing with the cell membrane and releasing their contents outside the cell.
 
• Exocytosis is essential for various cellular functions, including neurotransmitter release, hormone secretion, and the removal of cellular waste.
 
• It is a form of active transport, requiring energy in the form of ATP to proceed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endocytosis** is the reverse process of exocytosis, where cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane.
 
• There are different types of endocytosis, including phagocytosis (ingestion of large particles) and pinocytosis (ingestion of fluids and dissolved small molecules).
 
• **Apoptosis** refers to programmed cell death, a regulated sequence of events that leads to the elimination of cells without releasing harmful substances into the surrounding area.
 
• Both exocytosis and endocytosis are critical for maintaining cellular homeostasis and communication.

questions.question: Bharatanatyam of Tamil Nadu has grown out of the art of dancers dedicated to temples, and was earlier known:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sadir**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sadir** was the original name of Bharatanatyam, the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu.
 
• Bharatanatyam evolved from the art of temple dancers known as **Devadasis**, who were dedicated to serving the deities through dance.
 
• This dance form is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate footwork, and expressive hand gestures (mudras).
 
• It was redefined and renamed as Bharatanatyam in the 20th century, which helped in its revival and popularization beyond temple precincts.
 
• Bharatanatyam is now a well-respected and widely performed dance form both in India and internationally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The dance form is traditionally performed by women, but male dancers are also increasingly participating.
 
• Bharatanatyam performances typically include a series of dances (items) that are set to South Indian classical music.
 
• The training for Bharatanatyam is rigorous and often begins at a young age, encompassing both theoretical and practical aspects of the art form.
 
• The dance form has a rich repertoire of compositions and is often used to depict stories from Hindu mythology, epics, and scriptures.
 
• Bharatanatyam has been recognized as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

questions.question: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for a term of how many years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Members of the Rajya Sabha** are elected for a term of **6 years**.
 
• Rajya Sabha, also known as the **Council of States**, is the upper house of the Parliament of India.
 
• Unlike the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha is a **permanent body** and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
• Members are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies, and by the members of the Electoral college for Union Territories, using a single transferable vote system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Rajya Sabha was constituted on **3rd April 1952**.
 
• It represents the states and union territories of India.
 
• The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• To be a member of Rajya Sabha, a person must be at least 30 years old, a citizen of India, and possess such other qualifications as may be prescribed by Parliament.
 
• The maximum strength of Rajya Sabha is **250 members**, out of which 238 members represent the States and Union territories, and 12 members are nominated by the President.

questions.question: The result of which of the following movements/satyagrahas was the abolishment of the Tinkathia System under which the farmers were asked to cultivate indigo in 3/20th of their holdings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran Satyagraha**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Champaran Satyagraha** was a significant movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1917.
 
• The main objective of this movement was to address the grievances of the farmers in Champaran, Bihar, who were forced to grow indigo on a portion of their land under the **Tinkathia System**.
 
• The farmers were required to cultivate indigo in 3/20th (approximately 15%) of their holdings, which was highly exploitative and detrimental to their economic interests.
 
• As a result of the Champaran Satyagraha, the British authorities were compelled to abolish the Tinkathia System, providing relief to the farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Champaran Satyagraha** marked the first active involvement of Mahatma Gandhi in the Indian freedom struggle and laid the foundation for future non-violent movements.
 
• Gandhi's approach of non-violent resistance and civil disobedience became a cornerstone of the Indian independence movement.
 
• This movement also highlighted the plight of the Indian farmers under British rule and brought national attention to their struggles.

questions.question: The north-west region of India receives rainfall in winter due to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**western disturbances**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Western disturbances** are responsible for the rainfall in the north-west region of India during winter.
 
• These are extratropical storms originating in the Mediterranean region that bring sudden winter rain and snow to the north-western parts of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Western disturbances are crucial for the Rabi crop season in India, particularly for wheat cultivation.
 
• They generally affect the weather pattern of the region from December to February.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Western disturbances typically move from west to east, crossing Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan before entering India.
 
• The term 'western disturbance' was coined by Indian meteorologists to describe the phenomenon.
 
• These disturbances are more frequent and stronger during La Niña years.
 
• Besides causing rainfall, they are also associated with cold waves and foggy conditions in northern India.
 
• The intensity and frequency of western disturbances can vary each year, influencing the overall winter precipitation in the region.

• It aims to balance the need for development with the need to conserve forests by imposing stringent restrictions on the dereservation of forests and the use of forest land for non-forest purposes.
 
• The Act has been instrumental in preventing the indiscriminate destruction of forests and has contributed significantly to forest conservation in India.
 
• Over the years, various amendments have been made to the Act to address emerging challenges and to strengthen forest conservation efforts.

questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy strive to make India ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a welfare state**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy aim to establish India as a **welfare state**.
 
• These principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution of India and are intended to guide the state in formulating policies and laws.
 
• They emphasize social and economic democracy, aiming to reduce inequalities and ensure a decent standard of living for all citizens.
 
• Key areas include providing adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, protection of children and youth, and securing a social order based on justice and equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• The principles are inspired by the Irish Constitution and the objective is to create a social framework that supports the well-being of all citizens.
 
• Though non-justiciable, the principles act as a moral compass for the state in creating laws and policies aimed at social welfare and public good.
 
• The implementation of these principles is seen as crucial for achieving the goals of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity as enshrined in the Preamble of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following kings of Tuluva dynasty assumed the title of ‘Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishnadevaraya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Krishnadevaraya** was a prominent king of the Tuluva dynasty who ruled the Vijayanagara Empire from 1509 to 1529.
 
• He assumed the title of **'Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya'**, which signifies his efforts in establishing control over territories previously held by the Yavanas (foreigners).
 
• Krishnadevaraya is considered one of the greatest rulers in Indian history due to his military prowess, administrative acumen, and patronage of arts and literature.
 
• His reign is often regarded as the golden age of the Vijayanagara Empire, marked by extensive territorial expansion and cultural achievements.
 
• He was a patron of Telugu, Kannada, and Sanskrit literature and initiated several architectural projects, including the famous Vithala Temple in Hampi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tuluva dynasty** was the third dynasty to rule the Vijayanagara Empire, following the Sangama and Saluva dynasties.
 
• Krishnadevaraya's reign is well-documented by several contemporary sources, including the writings of Portuguese travelers such as Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz.
 
• He was succeeded by his half-brother Achyuta Deva Raya after his death in 1529.
 
• Krishnadevaraya's military campaigns included successful expeditions against the Bahmani Sultanate, the Gajapatis of Odisha, and the Portuguese, solidifying his dominance in the Deccan region.

questions.question: Which of the following kings took the title of ‘Dakshinapatheshvara’ (lord of the south) after defeating Harshvardhan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakeshin II**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pulakeshin II** took the title of 'Dakshinapatheshvara' after defeating Harshvardhan.
 
• He was a notable ruler of the **Chalukya dynasty** in the Deccan region of India.
 
• Pulakeshin II ruled from **610-642 CE** and is considered one of the greatest kings of ancient India.
 
• His victory over Harshvardhan marked a significant moment in the history of the Deccan region, establishing the Chalukyas as a dominant power.
 
• The title 'Dakshinapatheshvara' signifies his control over the southern territories, which was a notable accomplishment during his reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Chalukya dynasty** was known for its contributions to art, architecture, and culture.
 
• Pulakeshin II's reign is particularly noted for the construction of the rock-cut cave temples of **Badami**.
 
• He maintained diplomatic relations with foreign powers, including the **Persian Empire**.
 
• His court was adorned with scholars and poets, contributing to the cultural richness of his reign.
 
• Pulakeshin II's legacy continues to be remembered as a period of prosperity and cultural development in the Deccan region.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Kailashnath Temple, Ellora.

1. It is built completely in the Dravidian style.

2. Its main deity is Lord Shiva.

3. This temple was carved out of a portion of a hill.

4. It was built during the Chola phase at Ellora.

Which of the given statements is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1, 2 and 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kailashnath Temple** at Ellora is indeed a marvel of ancient Indian architecture.
 
• This temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva**, making statement 2 correct.
 
• The temple was **carved out of a single rock** from a hill, thus supporting statement 3.
 
• The temple is built in the **Dravidian style** of architecture, which supports statement 1.
 
• However, it was built during the **Rashtrakuta dynasty** and not during the Chola phase, making statement 4 incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Kailashnath Temple** is considered one of the largest rock-cut temples in the world.
 
• It is part of the Ellora Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The temple was commissioned by the Rashtrakuta king **Krishna I** in the 8th century.
 
• The Dravidian architectural style is characterized by its pyramid-shaped towers and intricate carvings.
 
• The temple complex includes elaborate sculptures, courtyards, and shrines.
